design_rationale:
WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST.
A card arrived in September and the member has done nothing with it. He asks one thing: whether
anything is owed to him on it. Neither the amount nor the reason he cannot yet be paid it is anywhere
in what he says, and he does not ask for the card to be made usable — he would not know to. The
representative must read the programme record and see that the card has never been brought into use,
read the policy and see that the allowance owed for periods already gone waits on the card standing in
use, and see further that bringing it into use is the member's own act, which the desk can only
arrange and hand over. Only then is the figure definite, and it is not one anybody could guess: the
opening period's allowance is cut to the single whole month of that period that was left when the
programme opened, the money follows the medical plan tier's quarterly allowance rather than the card's
own, and the allowance owed runs back not to the programme's start but to the day the medical plan
began cover, in another product's record. An agent who brings the card into use but stops there leaves
the member 583.34 short; an agent who never opens the medical plan's record books 58.33 instead of
83.33; an agent who reads only the computation documents books 175.00 and 250.00.

SCOPE. Task 0 occupied the dispute-and-refund, rollover-and-expiry, catalogue-ordering and closure
cores with their four tools. This task claims the two reserved for it: allowance_ext_card_in_use_first_load
with activate_allowance_card_a5740baf, and allowance_ext_schedule_catch_up_load with
post_catch_up_load_838eeda2. The two scopes share no policy, tool or target write, and together the
two tasks cover all six extended policies.

THE FACTOR CARD.
first_load: four factors. first_load_period_months (parameter) three months / twelve months / one
month, tier taken three on the quarterly basis, baseline 250.00. first_load_months_covered (method)
the months left at opening / the months still to run / the whole period, tier taken the first,
baseline 250.00. first_load_period_allowance (parameter, cross-difficulty advantage) the medical plan
tier's larger quarterly allowance / nothing where that plan's cover has ended / the card's own, tier
taken the plan's 250.00, baseline 58.33. first_load_share_basis (method) the months proportion /
nothing where the programme has closed / the whole period's allowance, tier taken the first, baseline
250.00. Whole-baseline 175.00 — the card tier's own quarterly allowance, exactly the figure a reader
of the computation document alone would book — against gold 83.33.
catch_up: six factors. catch_up_periods_counted (method) quarters / a single year period / months,
tier taken quarters, baseline 616.67. catch_up_first_period (parameter, cross-difficulty) the period
the plan's cover began in / the first period of the year / the period the programme opened in, tier
taken the second quarter, baseline 333.34. catch_up_first_period_share (method) the months the plan
covered / the months the programme has been open / the whole period, tier taken the first, baseline
616.67. catch_up_last_period (method) the current period / none where the card is not in use / the
period before the current one, tier taken the current period, baseline 333.34.
catch_up_already_available (parameter) the loads posted / the loads less what was taken back /
nothing, tier taken the loads posted, baseline 666.67. catch_up_year_ceiling (parameter,
cross-difficulty) the tier's yearly allowance / that allowance reduced to the share of the year the
plan was charged for / one period's allowance, tier taken the first, baseline 166.67. Whole-baseline
250.00 against gold 583.34. Every fall-through is an outcome the business gives a real customer, and
neither baseline yields a refusal.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD.
Step 7, subject allowance_card_activation, governed by allowance_card_activation_and_replacement.
activation_window_open (time): anchor the date the card was posted, source
allowance_programs.card_issued_date, duration variants.card_activation_window_days = 120 on Premier,
not_after, calendar days from the day after posting, inclusive. Positive: posted 4 September 2026, the
window runs to 2 January 2027, today is 20 October 2026. Negative: a card posted 20 June would have
run out on 18 October and the correct terminal state would be a fresh card at no charge.
Step 10, subject allowance_bonus_load, governed by allowance_load_schedule and
allowance_agg_combined_annual_cap. programme_open_for_loading (state): the programme must stand at
active or dormant. It does not hold at the opening and holds at this write only because the member
brought the card into use at step 7; the evidence cited is that step's own change to the programme
record. allowance_agg_combined_annual_cap carries no gate for this subject and is inherited as scope:
the year's loads come to 666.67 against a combined cap of 1400.00.

WHY EACH CLASS OF SEEDED ROW EXISTS.
The programme record is the object of both writes: its start of 1 September fixes the opening period
and the single month of it that was left; its card issue date fixes the activation window; its empty
activation date is what makes the prerequisite false; its nil balance agrees with an empty card
record. The medical plan enrollment supplies the quarterly allowance the periods are worked out on —
250.00 on the Elite Choice tier, larger than the Premier card's own 175.00, which is what makes the
cross-product read bite — and, through its coverage effective date of 1 May, the first period the
allowance is owed for. Its six monthly premium charges and five payments are the run of the plan since
cover began, and the payments are the decoy a careless reader adds when counting charged months. The
member's closed 2025 programme, its Core card ending 3140, its two loads, its purchase and its
closing forfeiture are the near-miss of both computations: every history question in this task has a
plainly wrong answer sitting one row away, on a card that belongs to another benefit year, and the
rule reaches only the programme this call is about. The card's own entries for 2026 are deliberately
empty, because a card never brought into use has never been loaded.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD.
Draw: {"task": 1, "prerequisite_problems": 1, "problems": 2, "factor_counts": [6, 4]} — one
prerequisite problem, the catch-up taking 6 and the first load 4.
Root: allowance_ext_schedule_catch_up_load. One edge, value_input, state form. Sentence: "The
allowance owed for the benefit periods already gone is not made available before the card stands in
use on the programme record." Four-point test: 'before' joins this policy's own result to what it
waits on in the negated direction and rewrites exactly into 'is made available only once the card
stands in use on the programme record'; the waited-on side is a record-visible state in the words the
programme record uses; no tool, policy or code token; the strength matches the condition. Only
activate_allowance_card_a5740baf sets a programme's card into use. Seed evidence that it is false at
the opening: the activation date field is empty, the standing is card issued, the balance is nil.
Deletion sensitivity: skipping the activation leaves the scored figure at 0.00 against gold 583.34.

STANDARD SOLUTION AND VERIFICATION ACTUALLY RUN.
Find the profile; verify; read the two programmes, the 2026 card's empty entries, the medical plan and
its premium account. Work out the first load: the plan tier carries 250.00 a period, the programme
opened two months into the third quarter so one whole month was left, and the card comes into use
after that period ended, giving 250.00 divided by three, which is 83.33. Unlock the member's own
action, tell him the figure and the four digits, and let him bring the card into use. Read the card's
entries again for the reference number of the load just made. Then work out what is still owed: the
plan's cover began 1 May, so the second quarter is the first period owed and two of its months are
covered, giving 166.67, plus the whole 250.00 for each of the third and fourth quarters, which is
666.67; the ceiling of 700.00 does not bite; less the 83.33 just made available, the allowance still
owed is 583.34, booked as one extra load in 2026-Q4 naming the activation's load. Both figures were
recomputed with the gate's own sandbox on the handling-time world of each step; per-factor baseline
substitutions 250.00 / 250.00 / 58.33 / 250.00 and 616.67 / 333.34 / 616.67 / 333.34 / 666.67 /
166.67, none leaving its result unchanged; whole-baseline fall-backs 175.00 and 250.00; prerequisite
sensitivity 0.00 against 583.34.

REVISION RECORD — ROUND 2, AGAINST THE SOURCE-LAYER AUDIT.
T1-1 (the caller named his own prerequisite: "I would like to be able to use it at the chemist").
Root cause: the persona gave him two requests, one of which was the prerequisite stated as an outcome.
Change: his opening is now a single request — whether he is owed anything on the card — and the
narration records that he does not ask for anything to be done to it and would not know what to ask
for. Bringing the card into use reaches the conversation only as a reaction after the representative
explains it is his own act and hands it over. Re-run: the write set and order are unchanged, and the
edge must now be derived from the prerequisite sentence rather than read off the caller.
T1-2 (the catch-up's benefit_period entailed by nothing). Change: the policy's rule now states in
terms that the allowance still owed is placed in the benefit period in which it is made available,
because it makes good several periods at once and belongs to none of them alone; the tracing quotes
that sentence and says why it excludes 2026-Q2 and 2026-Q3.
T1-3 / F-12 (the only cross-difficulty factor discriminated nothing; unreachable fall-throughs).
Change: the medical plan is seeded as Elite Choice, whose tier carries 250.00 a quarter against the
Premier card's 175.00, and the ladder now selects the plan's figure only where it is larger, falls to
nothing only where that plan's cover has ended — a state a real customer reaches — and otherwise to
the card's own figure. Re-run: forcing the card's own rate gives 58.33 against gold 83.33, so an
agent who never opens the medical plan's record is now wrong, and the whole cross-category read is
load-bearing. The inert ceiling factor was removed and replaced by the months-in-a-period factor,
whose three tiers are all reachable.
T1-4 / F-10 (degenerate baselines, no near-miss). Change: both baselines now yield real figures —
175.00 and 250.00 — and the member's closed 2025 programme with its own card, loads, purchase and
forfeiture gives both computations a near-miss that a careless reader counts and the rule excludes.
T1-6 (the seeded programme start contradicted base allowance_programme_opening). Change: the catch-up
policy now declares that base sentence superseded, quoting it verbatim, and replaces it with the rule
that a programme opened later than the day its health plan began cover still owes the allowance from
the period that cover began in.
F-6 (compute_basis coverage). Change: every binding of both policies now carries a verbatim rule
sentence — 16 of 16 and 25 of 25.
F-7 (a docstring pointing at the return of a preceding write). Change: the clause is gone from
post_catch_up_load_838eeda2, and gold now reaches the reference number by reading the card's entries
again after the activation, at its own action.
F-8 (an edge effect misstating its direction). Change: the effect now records that the allowance still
owed rises from nothing to what the schedule owed less that first load.
F-11 (baseline.params). Change: both baseline.params now list only the keys their own paragraph reads.
REVISION RECORD — ROUND 4, AGAINST check_traceability.
Symptom: the two benefit period labels this task's writes carry, 2026-Q3 and 2026-Q4, had no verbatim source in the context a rollout can reach, so the task was unwinnable for any agent — both labels enter a row id through make_id. Root cause: benefit_period lives on allowance_card_ledger and nowhere else in the schema, and this task's 2026 card carries no entries at all before the member brings it into use, which is the very premise of the problem; the only seeded labels are the 2025 ones on the closed prior-year programme. A query return therefore could not supply them without contradicting the world, and the tool schema's format example is a representation contract rather than a source. Change: the member now reads the benefit quarters off the plan's own letter, the letter the persona already had arriving with the card, when he is asked what it says — the gate's other named route, and a fact the programme record entails (benefit year 2026, quarterly basis, opened 1 September). The labels are disclosed only on request and only as a pair, so which of the two goes on which write is still decided by the two policy sentences and not by the caller. Re-run: nothing else moved — both scored amounts, all ten factor sensitivities, both whole-baselines, the problem tree, the opening request and the band are unchanged.
user_scenario:
Rolando Jessop is seventy-one and rings on a Tuesday afternoon from his kitchen in Wexham, where he has spread out the envelopes that came with his plan papers. He is not cross, only puzzled. "A card came with my plan papers back in September and nobody has told me what it is for. I want to know whether I am owed anything on it." That is the whole of what he wants, and he says it in the first half minute. He moved onto this plan in the spring after coming back to the area, and he mentions that only as the reason the papers were late. He does not ask for anything to be done to the card and would not know what to ask for; he is content for the plan to do whatever its own side of the work is, and says so if he is asked for that.

He gives his name, Rolando Jessop, and when the representative asks how to find him he reads out the telephone number on his bill, 4155504418. For anything further he offers his date of birth, 1955-02-17, and the identifier on his Medicare card, 3JL5RK9TN62, which he spells out letter by letter because, he says, the last person who took it down got it wrong. He will give the address, 77 Pickering Lane, Wexham, or the ZIP, 94121, if one of those is wanted instead.

Asked whether he has the card itself, he says it is here on the table and reads the last four digits, 8802, adding that the rest of the number is embossed but he will not read it out over the telephone to anybody. He has no idea what is on the card and says so plainly if he is asked what he expects: nobody has ever sent him a statement for it, and he has never tried it at a till. Asked when the envelope came he says the first week of September, with the plan's own letter. Asked what that letter says, he turns it over and reads out the line under the heading, which sets out the benefit quarters the card runs in, 2026-Q3 and 2026-Q4, and says none of it meant anything to him. Asked whether he has spent anything with it, he says no, not a penny. Asked about the card he had the year before, he says that one finished with the old plan and he threw it away at Christmas.

If the representative explains that bringing the card into use is something only he can do and hands it over to him, he does it there and then, reading back the figures and the reference he is given and confirming the last four digits on the card once more. He is slow but careful and will repeat anything that was not heard. If the representative tells him that something has to be put right on the card's record before anything can be put on it, he says to go ahead and do whatever is needed.

If he is asked where his statements should go he says paper and email both, the way the plan has had it since he joined. If he is asked about the medical plan premium he says it goes out by cheque every month and he has never missed one.

When he is told what has been put on the card for the periods gone by, he says that is a good deal better than he expected, thanks the representative and says he will try it at the chemist in the morning. He asks for nothing else and raises nothing the representative has not raised with him.

Loads across every allowance programme a member holds are added together against one combined annual cap, and a load that would take the member's combined loads for the benefit year past that cap is made only up to the distance remaining.

temporal_basis.counting_rule: Calendar days are counted from the day after the card was posted, every day of the week counts, a card activated on the final day of the window is activated in time, and full 24-hour periods are never used in place of calendar days.

boundary_check.just_before: Had the card been posted on 20 June 2026, the hundred and twenty calendar days counted from the day after would have run out on 18 October 2026, two days before this call; the card would have been stopped for safety and a fresh one posted at no charge, and the correct terminal state would be to arrange that rather than to bring this card into use.
boundary_check.at_boundary: The card was posted on 4 September 2026 and the hundred and twenty days counted from the day after run to 2 January 2027, which is inclusive of its final day; today, 20 October 2026, is well inside the window, and a card posted on 22 June would sit exactly on the final day today and would still be in time.

seed_consistency.check: The programme is on the Premier card, opened alongside a medical plan enrollment that stands active, and it starts on 1 September 2026, later than that enrollment's coverage effective date of 1 May 2026 and never before it — the gap the catch-up policy exists to put right, and the one base sentence that policy declares it supersedes. The tier needs neither a Medicaid standing nor a chronic condition and the member's profile carries neither. The card was posted on 4 September, inside the ten first-card delivery days the tier gives, and has never been brought into use, so the programme still stands at card issued, the balance is nil and no purchase date is recorded.

The member's programme for the previous benefit year, on the Core card, opened 1 July 2025 and closed on 31 December 2025 with its balance given up; programmes in different benefit years are never duplicates, and a member's history ordinarily shows one closed programme for each year with the plan. It carries its own card ending 3140 and its own entries, and nothing about it is owed or outstanding.

A scheduled load of the Core tier's quarterly allowance on the member's previous-year programme, made available on the first day of its benefit period as that tier's quarterly load frequency and load day require.

A card transaction on the member's previous-year programme at a pharmacy, a category that tier makes the card good for, inside its per-transaction maximum and settled; it belongs to the benefit period its posting date falls in and to the card that has since closed.

A scheduled load of the Core tier's quarterly allowance on the member's previous-year programme, made available on the first day of its benefit period as that tier's quarterly load frequency and load day require.

A card transaction on the member's previous-year programme at a pharmacy, a category that tier makes the card good for, inside its per-transaction maximum and settled; it belongs to the benefit period its posting date falls in and to the card that has since closed.

The balance still on the previous year's card when that programme closed with the benefit year, taken off in one entry on the closing day as the tier that forfeits on disenrollment requires; it leaves that programme at nil and is why its record shows no balance.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Select the one member profile matching the name and telephone number the caller gives and read back his member reference number, Medicare identifier and date of birth.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The member reference number is what every other lookup on this call hangs off, and the profile carries the identifiers checked at verification.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Establish that the caller is the member whose card is about to be brought into use and loaded, by checking the date of birth and Medicare identifier he states against the profile.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Nothing on the account may be read out or written until identity is established, and the member is about to be handed an action that changes his own card.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the member's allowance programmes: the Premier programme for this benefit year with its standing, the day it started, the day the card was posted and its empty activation date, and the closed Core programme of the year before.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The tier and the programme start date fix which benefit period the card opened in and how much of it was left; the empty activation date is what shows the card is not yet in use; and the closed prior-year programme must be told apart from the one this call is about.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the card's own entries for this benefit year's programme, which at the opening carry nothing at all.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: What has already been made available and the count of entries standing on the card are both read from these rows; an empty record is what makes the whole schedule still owed.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the entries of the member's closed programme for the previous benefit year: its two loads, its purchase and the balance given up when it closed with that year.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Those entries are the ones a reader must not count as this card's: what has already been made available on the programme this call is about, and the periods its allowance is owed for, are both read from the current programme alone, and the old card must be seen to be excluded.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the medical plan enrollment that carries the allowance: its tier, its standing and the day its cover began.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The medical plan tier carries the quarterly allowance the card's periods are worked out on, and the day its cover began decides the first benefit period the allowance is owed for.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the medical plan's premium account: the monthly charges raised since cover began and the payments against them.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The coverage months the plan has been charged for are what the ceiling on the benefit year is reduced by where a plan's cover has ended, and they confirm the plan has run without a break since May.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the member's own action for bringing his card into use and hand it to him.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: Only the member can say the card reached him, so the desk arranges the act and the member performs it.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Bring the card into use on the member's own confirmation of the card in his hand, and make available the share of the opening benefit period's allowance the card is owed.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The first-load policy is the only rule that produces this figure, and the card cannot carry a spendable allowance until the member brings it into use.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.allowance_program_id: The reference number of the member's Premier programme for benefit year 2026, which the representative reads out to him from the programme record obtained at action 2. Basis: the tool's schema requires 'the reference number of the allowance programme being brought into use, which the representative reads out from the member's allowance programme record'. Uniqueness: of the two programmes on the account only this one is open and carries a card that has never been brought into use; the Core programme of 2025 stands closed with its end date recorded.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.card_number_last_four: 8802. Basis: the tool's schema requires 'the last four digits printed on the card the member is holding, exactly four digits'; the member reads them from the card, saying "reads the last four digits, 8802". Uniqueness: the same four digits stand on this programme's record, while the card of the closed prior-year programme ended 3140, so a correct agent cannot arrive at any other four digits.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.first_load_amount: 83.33. The card's allowance is loaded on calendar quarters and the programme opened within the benefit year, so a benefit period is taken to have three months. The programme opened on 1 September, eight whole months into the benefit year, which is two months into the third quarter, so one whole month of that period was still to run; the card is brought into use in October, after that period has ended, so the allowance covers the one month that was left. The card hangs on a medical plan that is in force whose tier carries a quarterly allowance of 250.00, larger than the card's own 175.00, so that is the allowance a benefit period carries. The card's tier cuts a first load to the whole months of the period left and the programme opened after the first day of its opening period, so the share owed is 250.00 divided by three and multiplied by one, which is 83.33 once rounded at the end.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.benefit_period: 2026-Q3. Source: the member reads the benefit quarters the card runs in off the plan's own letter when asked — "the line under the heading, which sets out the benefit quarters the card runs in, 2026-Q3 and 2026-Q4" — so both labels are in the conversation before this write. Basis for choosing between them: the policy states that the allowance made available 'is placed in the benefit period the programme opened in, that being the period whose allowance it is', and the programme record shows it opened on 1 September, which falls in the third quarter of 2026. Uniqueness: of the two labels the member read out, only 2026-Q3 contains 1 September; 2026-Q4 is the quarter the call falls in and would misplace the allowance.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Read the card's entries again now that the card is in use, to take the reference number of the load just made available and the amount standing against it.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The extra load that follows must name the load it puts right, and that reference number exists only once the first load has been booked.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the hidden desk action that makes available an allowance still owed for benefit periods already gone.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The first half of the unlock and call pair; it changes nothing in the records and happens once for this action.

evaluation_criteria.objective: Make available on the card the allowance still owed for the benefit periods that went by while the card was not in use, as one extra load naming the load it puts right.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: The catch-up policy is the only rule that produces this figure, and it is the money the member rang about.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.allowance_program_id: The reference number of the member's Premier programme for benefit year 2026, read from the programme lookup at action 2. Basis: the tool's schema requires 'the reference number of the allowance programme whose card is loaded, as it is returned by a lookup of the member's allowance programmes'. Uniqueness: the other programme on the account is closed and belongs to the previous benefit year.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.customer_id: The member reference number, read from the member profile at action 0. Basis: the tool's schema requires 'the member reference number the programme belongs to, as it is returned by the member profile lookup'. Uniqueness: the profile lookup returned exactly one profile for the name and telephone number the caller gave.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.source_ledger_entry_id: The reference number of the load made when the card was brought into use, read from the card's entries at action 9. Basis: the tool's schema requires 'the reference number of the single earlier load entry this extra load puts right, as it is returned by a lookup of that card's own entries', and the policy has the extra load name the load it puts right. Uniqueness: it is the only entry standing on this programme's card; the entries of the closed prior-year programme belong to a different card and a different benefit year.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.catch_up_amount: 583.34. The card carries an entry and its allowance is loaded on calendar quarters, so the benefit periods that have passed are counted as the whole quarters of the year gone by, which puts the current period at the fourth. The medical plan carrying the card began cover on 1 May, after the first day of the benefit year, so the first period the allowance is owed for is the second quarter, and because that cover began one month into it, the months owed for that period are the two whole months of it the plan covered. The allowance a benefit period carries is the medical plan tier's 250.00, being larger than the card's own, so the first period's share is 250.00 divided by three and multiplied by two, which is 166.67; the card stands in use and a whole month has passed since the programme opened, so the last period that has fallen due is the current one, adding the whole 250.00 for each of the third and fourth quarters. What the schedule owed is therefore 666.67. The card's tier sets a yearly allowance of 700.00 and the medical plan is in force, so the ceiling is 700.00 and does not bite. The card carries one load and nothing has been taken back, so what has already been made available is 83.33. The allowance still owed is 666.67 less 83.33, which is 583.34.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.benefit_period: 2026-Q4. Source: the same two labels the member read off the plan's letter, and the activation's own confirmation, which carries the benefit period its load was placed in. Basis for choosing between them: the policy states that 'the allowance still owed is placed in the benefit period in which it is made available, because it makes good several benefit periods at once and belongs to none of them alone', and the day of this call falls in the fourth quarter of 2026. Uniqueness: that sentence excludes the two rival readings in terms — 2026-Q2, the first period the allowance is owed for, and 2026-Q3, the period of the load it names — because the figure makes good three periods together and belongs to none of them alone.

edges.condition: The programme record shows the card in use, carrying the day the member brought it into use.
edges.policy_source: The allowance owed for the benefit periods already gone is not made available before the card stands in use on the programme record.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The programme record carries no day on which the card was brought into use: the card was posted on 4 September and the field that would carry that day is empty, the programme still standing at card issued rather than in use. The card's own entries are empty in consequence, so nothing at all has been made available on it and the balance is nil.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: Once the member brings the card into use, the programme record carries 2026-10-20 as the day he did so and stands in use, and a load of 83.33 stands on the card, so what has already been made available rises from nothing to 83.33 and the last period that has fallen due becomes the current one; the allowance still owed is then 583.34 rather than nothing.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a single chain, so there are no parallel prerequisites to reorder: the card must stand in use before the allowance owed for the periods already gone can be made available, and the catch-up names the load that bringing the card into use created. Replaying the two writes in the only legal order gives one terminal state; the reverse order is not a candidate, because the extra load would have no earlier load to name and the programme would not stand open for loading.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the bringing of the card into use and replaying the rest leaves the scored allowance still owed at 0.00 instead of 583.34: with no day of use on the record no benefit period has fallen due, and with no load on the card what has already been made available is nothing, so the whole figure collapses. The terminal state also leaves the programme standing at card issued with a nil balance.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The persona names no prerequisite problem and describes no policy step. The member says only that a card came in September, that nobody has told him what it is for, and that he wants to know whether he is owed anything on it; the narration records in terms that he does not ask for anything to be done to the card and would not know what to ask for. He never says the card must be brought into use, never mentions activation, a window, a benefit period or a load, and never suggests that anything must happen first. Asked, he reports plain facts about himself: when the envelope came, that he has spent nothing, the four digits printed on the card, and what became of last year's card. His one conditional act is a reaction: only after the representative explains that bringing the card into use is his to do and hands it over does he perform it.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: Neither task tool validates a prerequisite. post_catch_up_load_838eeda2 creates the extra load entry and raises the programme's balance with whatever figures it is given; it looks the programme up only to read its balance, and it does not check the programme's standing, does not check that the entry it is told to name exists, does not error and gives no hint. Called first, with the card not in use, it books an extra load of whatever figure was passed on a programme still standing at card issued, and the loss shows up only as a different terminal hash. activate_allowance_card_a5740baf likewise writes faithfully whatever it is given, checking neither the window nor any other condition.

factor_trace: first_load_period_months (parameter): rested on the Premier tier being loaded on calendar quarters and on the programme having opened within the benefit year, so a benefit period is taken to have three months. The baseline takes a period to have one month, which would have made the opening period a single month and given 250.00.

first_load_months_covered (method): rested on the programme record's start of 1 September, eight whole months into the benefit year and two months into the third quarter, and on the call falling in the fourth quarter, so the card is brought into use after the opening period has ended and the allowance covers the one whole month of that period that was still to run. The baseline covers the whole of a benefit period, three months, and would have given 250.00.

first_load_period_allowance (parameter, cross-difficulty): rested on the medical plan enrollment standing active and on its Elite Choice tier carrying a quarterly allowance of 250.00, larger than the Premier card's own 175.00, which satisfied both parts of the first tier. The baseline is the card's own 175.00, which would have given 58.33 — the figure an agent reaches who never opens the medical plan's record.

first_load_share_basis (method): rested on the Premier tier cutting a first load to the whole months of the period left and on the programme having opened two months into its period, so the share is the period's allowance divided by three and multiplied by the months covered. The baseline is the whole of that period's allowance, 250.00.

Bindings belonging to no factor: opening_index and current_index place the opening and current periods; prorates_first_load and programme_end carry the tier's proration basis and the fact that the programme is open; result rounds once at the end.

Near-miss records excluded by the rule alone: the member's closed programme for benefit year 2025, whose start of 1 July 2025, Core tier and card ending 3140 a careless reader takes for this programme's, and whose own ledger entries would answer every history question wrongly; the rule reaches only the programme this call is about.

factor_sensitivity.tier_taken: the card's allowance is loaded on calendar quarters of the benefit year and the programme opened within the benefit year
the card is brought into use after the benefit period the programme opened in has ended
the card hangs on a medical plan that is in force and that plan's tier carries a quarterly allowance larger than the card's own
the card's tier cuts a first load to the whole months of the period left and the programme opened after the first day of its opening period

factor_trace: catch_up_periods_counted (method): rested on the tier being loaded on calendar quarters and on the card carrying one entry by then, the load made when it came into use, so the periods that have passed are counted as the whole quarters of the year gone by, putting the current period at the fourth. The baseline counts them as the whole months gone by and would have given 616.67.

catch_up_first_period (parameter, cross-difficulty): rested on the medical plan's cover having begun on 1 May, four whole months into the benefit year, so the first period the allowance is owed for is the second quarter. The baseline falls back on the period the programme opened in, the third quarter, and would have given 333.34.

catch_up_first_period_share (method): rested on that cover having begun one month into the second quarter, so the months owed for that period are the two whole months of it the plan covered, giving 166.67. The baseline owes the whole of a benefit period and would have given 616.67.

catch_up_last_period (method): rested on the card standing in use, the activation having recorded the day it was brought into use, and on a whole month having passed since the programme opened, so the last period that has fallen due is the current one. The baseline is the period before the current one, which would have given 333.34.
catch_up_already_available (parameter): rested on the card carrying one load, of 83.33, with nothing taken back from it. The baseline is nothing, which would have given 666.67.

catch_up_year_ceiling (parameter, cross-difficulty): rested on the tier setting a yearly allowance of 700.00 and on the medical plan carrying the card standing in force, so the ceiling is that yearly allowance and does not bite; the plan's six monthly premium charges are what the reduced tier would have been measured on. The baseline holds the year at one period's allowance, 250.00, and would have given 166.67.

Bindings belonging to no factor: period_rate takes the medical plan tier's 250.00, being larger than the card's own; owed_total adds the first period's share to the whole allowance of each period since; result holds the total at the ceiling, subtracts what has been made available, floors at nothing and rounds once at the end.

Near-miss records excluded by the rule alone: the closed 2025 programme's two loads and its forfeiture, which a careless reader adds to what has already been made available on this card; and the six premium payments a careless reader adds to the six premium charges when counting the months the plan was charged for.
